मैंने पहले भी कहा था, हम रिफॉर्म कंपलशन से नहीं, कन्विक्शन से कर रहे हैं। लक्ष्य को प्राप्त करने के लिए कर रहे हैं।

जब मैं यह विकसित भारत की बात कर रहा हूं, देश को तेज गति से आगे बढ़ाने की बात कर रहा हूं, उसका सबसे बड़ा लाभार्थी कौन है, इन सारे प्रयासों का सबसे बड़ा साधक कौन है, अगर साधक है तो मेरे देश का युवा है, मेरे देश की युवा शक्ति है। विकसित भारत की यात्रा में युवाओं की बहुत बड़ी भूमिका है। इतना ही नहीं, विकसित भारत का सबसे बड़ा लाभार्थी भी मेरे देश का युवा है और इसलिए हमें विकसित भारत के लक्ष्य को युवाओं के साथ जोड़कर के आगे बढ़ाना है। युवाओं हमारी सर्वोच्च प्राथमिकता के साथ हमें आगे बढ़ना है।

पिछले 10-12 साल में उस दिशा में बहुत कुछ हुआ है। स्टार्टअप इंडिया अभियान आज पूरे देश में ढाई लाख से ज्यादा registered स्टार्टअप्स बन गए हैं। देश के नौजवान, खुद तो काम कर रहे हैं, अनेकों को रोजगार दे रहे हैं। 1 लाख करोड़ रुपया, इनोवेशन फंड भारत सरकार ने घोषित किया है। मैं देश के नौजवानों को कहना चाहता हूं, आप अपने सपनों को लेकर के आइए, संसाधनों की कमी नहीं रहने देंगे। 1 लाख करोड़ रुपया, आपके दिल दिमाग को सामर्थ्य देने का एक व्यवस्था हमने कर दी है। रिसर्च के नए अवसर मिले, डिजिटल इंडिया के नए सस्ते डाटा, यह युवाओं को सशक्त किया है। दुनिया में सस्ता डाटा कहीं है, तो भारत की धरती पर है और देश के नौजवानों को उसने नई ताकत दी है। स्किल इंडिया हमने नेशनल प्रोग्राम बनाया है। स्पेस सेक्टर को हमने ओपन कर दिया। नेशनल ड्रोन पॉलिसी हमने बनाई है। खेलो इंडिया पॉलिसी बनाई है। 35 वर्षों तक एजुकेशन पॉलिसी नहीं थी, नई एजुकेशन पॉलिसी लेकर के आए हैं और इसका फायदा मिडिल क्लास के परिवारों को हुआ है।

2004 से 2014, आंकड़े मुझे देना चाहिए आपको। 2004 से 2014, हमारे देश में 350 से भी कम यूनिवर्सिटीज थी और आज 10-12 साल के भीतर-भीतर, करीब 650 नई यूनिवर्सिटीज जुड़ चुकी है। करीब 1000 का आंकड़ा हम पहुंच रहे हैं। 2014 के पहले मेडिकल की सिर्फ 400 सीटें हुआ करती थी, आज करीब-करीब 850 सीटें मेडिकल की हो रही है। इतना ही नहीं, अब विदेशी यूनिवर्सिटीज भी भारत की धरती पर आ रही है। भारत के अंदर विदेशी यूनिवर्सिटी की डिग्री मेरे नौजवान को मिले इसका प्रबंध भी हो चुका है। हमारे देश के युवा मन बचपन से ही टेक्नोलॉजी की तरफ आकर्षित हो, उस दिशा में हम काम कर रहे हैं और इसलिए हमने करीब 10,000 से अधिक अटल टिंकरिंग लैब छोटे-छोटे बच्चों के हवाले कर दी है, ताकि उनका इनोवेशन और टेक्नोलॉजी के अंदर उनका मन बने। हमने अनेक रास्ते खोले, हमने स्टार्टअप ओपन कर दिया। आपने देखा होगा, भारत के प्राइवेट स्टार्टअप 28 साल के एवरेज उम्र के बच्चों ने, नौजवानों ने, दुनिया में पहला, पहले ही ट्रायल में अपना सेटेलाइट लॉन्च कर दिया और रॉकेट लॉन्च कर दिया उन्होंने, बहुत बड़ा काम कर दिया।

आज करीब ढाई लाख से ज्यादा रजिस्टर्ड स्टार्टअप हैं। हमने पिछले दिनों एआई इंपैक्ट समिट किया था। एआई का विस्तार बहुत तेजी से बढ़ रहा है। लाल किले से मैं देश के नौजवानों के लिए घोषणा करना चाहता हूं। हमने तय किया है कि आने वाले एक वर्ष में 1 करोड़ युवाओं को एआई स्किल के लिए ट्रेनिंग देने का हम काम करेंगे ताकि हमारा देश का नौजवान एआई की दुनिया में भी नेतृत्व करने का सामर्थ्य हो।

बायोइकोनॉमी एक नया क्षेत्र है। एक समय था 2014 के पहले, सिर्फ 60,000 करोड़ रुपये का बायोइकोनमी का काम होता था। मेरे देश के नौजवान, आपने क्या कमाल कर दिया है। देखिए, नीतियां जब सही होती है, लक्ष्य जब साफ होता है, तो मेरे देश के नौजवान कैसा करके देते हैं। बायोइकोनॉमी में देश की युवा शक्ति ने सामर्थ्य दिखाया। 2014 के पहले जो 60 हजार करोड़ का कारोबार था, आज वो बायोइकोनॉमी 20 लाख करोड़ पहुंच चुकी है दोस्तों। 2009-10 का कालखंड था, सिर्फ 1.5 लाख डेढ़ लाख इलेक्ट्रिक व्हीकल बिके थे, 2009-10 में डेढ़ लाख इलेक्ट्रिक व्हीकल। इस 25-26 में 25 लाख इलेक्ट्रिक व्हीकल बिके हैं।

एविएशन सेक्टर भी मेरे नौजवानों के लिए बहुत तेजी से आगे बढ़ रहा है। नए एयरपोर्ट, नए रूट, नए-नए रोजगार के अवसर बना रहे हैं। मेंटेनेंस, ओवरहालिंग, इसके भी कारण देश में बहुत बड़ी मात्रा में skilled मैन पावर को काम मिल रहा है। मेड इन इंडिया हवाई जहाज बनाने की दिशा में हमने सफलता पाई है। मेड इन इंडिया डिफेंस ट्रांसपोर्ट एयरक्राफ्ट C295 ऑलरेडी अपनी उड़ान भर चुका है, सफल उड़ान भर चुका है। यह देश के नौजवानों के लिए, मेरे साथियों ड्रोन ने भी बहुत बड़ा काम किया है। स्वामित्व योजना गांव में ड्रोन से स्वामित्व योजना सफल हो रही है। करीब सवा तीन करोड़ परिवारों को स्वामित्व योजना का लाभ मिला है और इसके कारण 140 लाख करोड़ रुपये जैसी संपत्ति अनलॉक हुई है, जिसके कारण बैंक से लोन मिल सकता है, लोग अपना कारोबार कर सकते हैं।

हमारे मध्‍यम वर्गीय परिवारों के सामने एक बहुत बड़ा बोझ बन चुका है कोचिंग क्‍लासिस की स्‍पर्धा, हर मां-बाप को लग रहा है कि कोचिंग क्‍लास में बच्‍चे को नहीं भेजा, तो हम प्रतिष्‍ठित परिवार नहीं हैं। इन गरीब और मिडिल क्‍लास परिवारों की हम चिंता करते हुए हजारों-करोड़ रुपए का उनका खर्च है, वो भी बचे, बेटे भी अपने आस पास रह सके, उनकी देखभाल हो सके, परिवार पर आर्थिक बोझ न आए और इसलिए हमने युवाओं के लिए विभिन्न परीक्षाओं की फ्री ऑनलाइन कोचिंग हमने करने का निर्णय किया है, डिजिटल पब्लिक इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर है, हमारे पास उत्तम टैलेंट है, टीचर्स हैं, उन संसाधनों को जोड़ करके हम देश के नौजवानों को फ्री कोचिंग देने का एक पूरा नेटवर्क हम खड़ा करने वाले हैं।

मैं हमेशा कहता आया हूं, जो खेले, वह खिले। जब मैं खेले, वो खिले की बात कर रहा हूं, तब मेरे प्यारे देशवासियों, आज भारत खेल की दुनिया में अपनी जगह बना रहा है। अब खेल के पोडियम में भारत का राष्ट्रीय गीत सुनाई देता है, भारत का राष्ट्रगान सुनाई देता है, भारत का तिरंगा झंडा लहराता नजर आ रहा है। टॉप्स योजना ने बहुत बड़ी सफलता पाई है। खेलो इंडिया गेम्स, यूनिवर्सिटी गेम्स, विंटर गेम्स, बीच गेम्स, स्पोर्ट्स इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर, स्पोर्ट्स के लिए कोचिंग, स्पोर्ट्स मेडिसिन, स्पोर्ट्स के लिए न्यूट्रिशन, इन सारे विषयों में भारत अब महारत हासिल करने की दिशा में आगे बढ़ रहा है। नौजवानों के लिए पूरा नया क्षेत्र खिलाड़ी ना बन सके, तो उसकी सपोर्ट सिस्टम में भी बहुत बड़ा क्षेत्र खुल रहा है। स्पोर्ट्स की दुनिया में भारत का प्रदर्शन बेहतर होता जा रहा है और हम 2036 में ओलंपिक के मजबूत दावेदार बनकर के आगे बढ़ रहे हैं, और 2030 में कॉमनवेल्थ गेम्स को भारत अब होस्ट करने वाला है।

और मेरे साथियों,

दुनिया में जो ओलंपिक के खेल होते हैं, करीब 40 प्रकार के गेम होते हैं और करीब 325-350 स्पर्धाएं होती हैं ओलंपिक में और आपको जानकर के दुख होगा मेरे देशवासियों। मेरे नौजवानों, मैं आपको चुनौती देता हूं, मैं आह्वान करता हूं, मैं आपकी मदद चाहता हूं, 325 जितने स्पर्धाओं में भारत दो तिहाई खेलों में कहीं होता ही नहीं है। हमारी मौजूदगी नहीं होती, हम क्वालीफाई नहीं होते हैं, हमने तय किया है कि 2036 में जो ओलंपिक होगा, हम चाहते हैं कि वो भारत में हो, लेकिन 2036 में जिन विधाओं में आज भारत खेलता नहीं है, जिन विधाओं में भारत क्वालीफाई नहीं करता है, जिन स्पर्धाओं में भारत ने छोड़ के रखा है, तीन चौथाई हिस्सा हमारे इंतजार कर रहा है, भारत उस पर बल देगा और इसके लिए हम टैलेंट हंट का एक अभियान भी चलाना चाहते हैं। हमें अगर 2036 के लिए खिलाड़ी चाहिए, तो आज जो 5 साल, 10 साल, 15 साल, की उम्र के यह नौजवान हैं, बेटे हैं, उनकी तरफ ध्यान देना होगा, उन बेटियों पर ध्यान देना होगा। और इसलिए 5 से 15 उम्र के बच्चों में खेल प्रतिभा ढूंढने के लिए गांव-गांव, शहर-शहर, स्कूल-स्कूल एक टैलेंट हंट का अभियान चलाया जाएगा, बच्चों की प्रतिभा को देखा जाएगा और फिर उनको स्पेशल ट्रेनिंग देकर के देश के लिए खेलने वाले अच्छे खिलाड़ी बनाए जाएंगे।

मेरे प्यारे युवा,

देश के सामने, देश के नौजवानों के सामने, नशा एक बहुत बड़ा संकट बनता जा रहा है। नशा मुक्त भारत, यह हम सबका सामूहिक दायित्व होना चाहिए। हमारे उज्ज्वल भविष्य के लिए हमारी युवा पीढ़ी मजबूत हो, हमारा युवा सामर्थ्य हमारे देश के लिए काम आए, इसलिए नशा मुक्त भारत, पिछले दिनों माय भारत के वालंटियर्स ने, देश के एनजीओस ने, देश के सामाजिक सांस्कृतिक संगठनों ने, देश के आध्यात्मिक पुरुषों ने मिलकर के नशा मुक्त भारत का 100 सप्ताह का एक कार्यक्रम तय किया है। 100 सप्ताह तक एक अभियान चलने वाला है। मैं हर परिवार को कहना चाहता हूं कि आप भी इस इस अभियान का हिस्सा बने, आप इसके साथ जुड़िए और देश के नशा मुक्त भारत के सपने को पूरा करने के लिए आप आगे आइए।

21वीं सदी में दशकों पुरानी जो चुनौतियां है, उन चुनौतियों को खत्म करना बहुत अनिवार्य है। नक्सलवाद, माओवाद ने लाखों युवाओं के भविष्य को तबाह कर दिया। अनेक माताओं के दूधमल नौजवानों को छीन लिया, बर्बाद कर दिया, हर मां-बाप के सपनों को चूर-चूर कर दिया। इस नक्सलवाद ने चार-चार दशक तक हिंदुस्तान के बहुत बड़े हिस्से को, बहुत बड़ी आबादी को दबोच करके रखा था, बंदूक के नोक पर दबोच करके रखा था, संविधान की धज्जियां उड़ा दी थी और देश के सामान्य नागरिकों की रक्षा में 3500 से ज्यादा हमारी पुलिस के सुरक्षा बल के जवान शहीद हो गए। युद्ध के अंदर जितने सैनिक मरते हैं, उससे ज्यादा हमारे पुलिस जवानों को जान की बाजी लगानी पड़ी, ताकि देश के सामान्य मानवी को सुरक्षा मिले। इस नक्सलवाद ने धरती को लहूलुहान कर दिया था। 2014 में आपने जब हमें मौका दिया, उसी दिन हमने संकल्प लिया था कि हम देश को नक्सलवाद से मुक्त करेंगे और आज मुझे खुशी है कि नक्सली माओवादी हिंसा आखिरी सांस भी शायद रहने की अब तो ताकत नहीं रही है, पूरी तरह उसे खत्म करने की दिशा में, जहां पर कभी नक्सलवादियों की गोलियां चलती थी, जहां पर कभी धरती रक्त रंजित रहा करती थी, आज उसी नक्सल क्षेत्रों में, उसी इलाकों में, नक्सल मुक्त होने के कारण विकास, विश्वास और प्रयास का तिरंगा लहरा रहा है।

लेकिन इस चुनौती को हमने कम नहीं आंकना है। इस चुनौती से हमें और भी सावधान रहने की जरूरत है। वर्षों तक देश की सत्ता में माओवादी सोच के लोग गलियारों में अपनी जगह बनाकर के बैठे थे। सरकारी कमेटियों में सलाहकार के रूप में भी ये माओवादी सोच ने नीतियों को प्रभावित किया था।

जंगलों में हमें हथियारी नक्सलों का खात्मा बुलाने में उस संकट से देश को मुक्त कराने में सफलता मिली है। लेकिन हथियारी नक्सल तो गए, लेकिन दिमागी नक्सल, यह दिमागी नक्सल मौके की तलाश में है। हिंसा अराजकता के वो रास्ते खोज रहे हैं। समाज को गलत राह पर घसीटने के लिए भांति-भांति के दांव कर रहे हैं। इन दिमागी नक्सलियों को पहचानना होगा। इन दिमागी नक्सलियों को आइसोलेट करना होगा और राष्ट्र को विकसित राष्ट्र बनाने की मुख्यधारा की ओर देश की युवा पीढ़ी को जोड़ना होगा।

सुरक्षित भारत बनाना हम सबका दायित्व है। चुनौती सीमा के भीतर हो या सरहद से बाहर भारत हर परिस्थिति के लिए तैयार है। आज युद्ध का नेचर बदल रहा है। अब युद्ध सीमा पर ही होता है यह गारंटी नहीं है। आज युद्ध सीमा के अंदर कहीं रिफाइनरी में जा करके, कहीं बैंकिंग सेक्टर को जाकर के, कहीं डाटा सेंटर को जाकर के, एक प्रकार से लड़ाई का नया रूप इंफ्रास्ट्रक्चर तोड़े जा रहे हैं, फैक्ट्रियां तोड़ी जा रही हैं। हमने मिशन सुदर्शन चक्र की पिछले सालों घोषणा की थी। बहुत तेजी से उस पर काम चल रहा है। आज डिफेंस एक्सपोर्ट हमारा करीब 50 गुना बढ़ा है। करीब 100 देशों में हमारे अस्त्र-शस्त्र पहुंच रहे हैं। वैश्विक पटल पर भारत की प्रतिष्ठा धीरे-धीरे बढ़ रही है। बदलते हुए समय में अस्त्र-शस्त्र की तरफ काम करना है, सैन्य बलों का सामर्थ्य बढ़ाना है। लेकिन साथ-साथ नागरिकों को भी तैयार करना होगा। पिछली शताब्दी के युद्धों के अनुरूप जो सिविल डिफेंस की व्यवस्थाएं हमारे देश में विकसित हुई है, वो कालबाह्य हो चुकी है और इसलिए मैं आज लाल किले से घोषणा कर रहा हूं कि, हम आने वाले दिनों में सिविल डिफेंस का एक वाइब्रेंट नेटवर्क खड़ा करेंगे। आधुनिक व्यवस्थाओं से उनको परिचित कराएंगे। आधुनिक संकटों से नागरिकों को रक्षा करने की क्या व्यवस्था हो सकती है, एक बहुत बड़ा वॉलंटरी फोर्स सिविल डिफेंस का आधुनिक चुनौतियों को पार करने वाला हम बनाने वाले हैं।

राष्ट्र के निर्माण में आज हमारी बहनों बेटियों का योगदान हम सबके लिए बहुत बड़ा प्रेरणा का कारण बना हुआ है। फाइटर जेट हो या सिविल एविएशन, हमारी बेटियां सबसे आगे दिखाई दे रही हैं। खेल कूद का मैदान हो, हमारी बेटियां आगे दिखाई दे रहीं हैं। स्टेम एजुकेशन में भर्ती होने की प्रक्रिया हो सबसे ज्यादा हमारी बेटियां आगे दिख रही हैं। आज सेना में भी एनडीए से जो बेटियां निकली हैं वो बड़े रौब के साथ देश की सेना का नेतृत्व करने का सामर्थ्य दिखाने लगी है। मेरी बेटियों की ताकत कैसी है, मैं पिछले दिनों सानंद में एक सेमीकंडक्टर प्लांट में गया था, वहां आदिवासी बेटियां देश के अलग-अलग कोने से आई हुई बेटियां काम कर रही थी। वो उस गांव से आई थी जिन्होंने पासपोर्ट क्या होता है पता तक नहीं था। वो बेटियां विदेशों में गईं, ट्रेनिंग लेकर के आईं और आज चीप निर्माण का काम कर रही हैं और बड़े कॉन्फिडेंस, मैंने जो उनका कॉन्फिडेंस देखा, मैं सचमुच में बहुत प्रभावित हुआ था। आज तीन 3 करोड़ बहनों को हमने लखपति दीदी बनाने का लक्ष्य तय किया था, उसको पार कर लिया। अब हम 6 करोड़ लखपति दीदी बनाने के लक्ष्य को लेकर के आगे बढ़ रहे हैं। 3 करोड़ नई लखपति दीदी बनना मतलब ग्रामीण अर्थव्यवस्था में बहुत बड़ा बदलाव मातृशक्ति के द्वारा आने वाला है।

आज पंचायतों में, नगर पालिका में, महानगर पालिका में, बहुत बड़ी मात्रा में हमारी महिलाएं जनप्रतिनिधि बनकर के देश का मार्गदर्शन कर रही हैं, समस्याओं का समाधान कर रही हैं, बहुत ही सक्षम नेतृत्व दे रही हैं और इसी को ध्यान में रखते हुए हमने पार्लियामेंट में नारी शक्ति वंदन अधिनियम पारित किया था। लेकिन किसी न किसी कारण से राजनीति के अखाड़े में पिछले 40 साल से यह सपना हमेशा राजनीतिक अखाड़े का शिकार हो गया है। मैं देश के सभी राजनीतिक दलों से आज लाल किले की प्राचीर से तिरंगे झंडे की छाया में खड़े होकर के प्रार्थना करता हूं, आग्रह करता हूं। आइए, उन महिलाओं के सामर्थ्य के पुजारी बनिए। उन महिलाओं के सम्मान में आगे आइए और जल्द से जल्द हमारी माताओं-बहनों को 33% विधानसभा और लोकसभा में उनको प्रतिनिधित्व मिले, वह भारत की नीति गढ़ करके अंदर अपना योगदान दें। समय की मांग है और मैं सभी राजनीतिक दलों से फिर से आग्रह करता हूं, आइए महिला आरक्षण लागू करके महिला सम्मान में आप भी जुड़िए, आप भी यश लीजिए, आप भी क्रेडिट लीजिए, लेकिन मेरी माताओं-बहनों को हक दीजिए।

विकसित भारत का संकल्प तभी पूरा होगा, जब विकास अंतिम व्यक्ति तक पहुंचेगा। 2014 से पहले सिर्फ 25 करोड़ लोगों के पास सोशल सिक्‍योरिटी का कवर था, सिर्फ 25 करोड़ के पास।

पिछले 5-7 दशक में सिर्फ 25 करोड़, हमने एक दशक के भीतर-भीतर 100 करोड़ देशवासियों को सोशल सिक्योरिटी का कवच दिया है। आयुष्मान भारत योजना से 70 साल की उम्र के बुजुर्गों से भी आज 5 लाख रुपये तक मुफ्त दवाई की व्यवस्था हो रही है। करोड़ों-करोड़ों परिवारों को इसके कारण बहुत बड़ी सुविधा मिली है और इस आयुष्मान कार्ड के कारण 2 लाख करोड़ रुपया जो दवाई और ऑपरेशन के पीछे खर्च होना था, वो मेरे परिवारों के बचे हैं, वो गरीब परिवार हैं, वो मध्यम वर्ग के परिवार हैं, उनको इतनी बड़ी मदद मिली है!

आज मुझे एक काम के लिए आपकी मदद चाहिए। मैं आप सबसे एक मदद मांग रहा हूं। सभी नौजवानों से मैं चाहता हूं कि आप इसका नेतृत्व करिए। आपका एक या दो घंटे देश को बहुत बड़ी शक्ति देने वाले हैं। आपको लगेगा एक दो घंटे में मैं देश की क्या शक्ति, मैं बताता हूं। आप बहुत बड़ी शक्ति बनने वाले हैं और इसलिए हर घर में वातावरण बने। इन दिनों देश में जनगणना का काम हो रहा है। Census का काम हो रहा है, गिनती चल रही है और गिनती सिर्फ आंकड़ों से बात बनती नहीं है। उसकी बारीकियों से नीतियां बनती हैं, योजनाएं बनती हैं, देश आगे बढ़ने की अपनी रूपरेखा तैयार करता है और इसलिए सटीक जानकारियां होना बहुत जरूरी है। कभी-कभी जो सरकार की तरफ से प्रतिनिधि आते हैं, वो इतनी जल्दी में होते हैं, कभी स्पेलिंग एक लिख देते हैं, कभी अलग लिख देते हैं और इसके कारण अल्टीमेटली परिणाम हमें सही मिलने में दिक्कतें आती है। अब जब टेक्नोलॉजी अवेलेबल है और इस बार निर्णय किया है आप स्वयं भी जनगणना में अपनी जानकारियां अपने मोबाइल फोन से भरकर के दे सकते हैं। बाद में कोई बाबू आएंगे, कोई प्रतिनिधि आएंगे, आपसे चर्चा करेंगे, लेकिन आप परिवार के सब बैठकर के अगर डिजिटली अपना रजिस्ट्री करवा दें, सारी बारीकियां स्पेलिंग में भी गलती ना हो, कोई भी जानकारियों में गलती ना हो, आप जितनी परफेक्ट जानकारी देंगे, देश को आगे बढ़ने में बहुत बड़ी मदद मिलेगी और इसलिए मैं देश के नौजवानों को कहता हूं कि आप अपने परिवार के लोगों को बिठा करके पूरे फॉर्म को समझिए। पहले कागज पर फॉर्म को भर दीजिए, कोई गलती है, तो करेक्ट कर लीजिए और फिर टेक्नोलॉजिकली उसको डिजिटली, इसको अपलोड कर दीजिए। आप देखिए, इतना बड़ा काम देश कर लेगा और देश का समय और शक्ति सही काम के लिए उपयोग आएगा और इसलिए मेरे देश के नौजवानों को जनगणना के इस काम में सक्रियता से जुड़ने के लिए मैं आग्रह करता हूं।

मेरे प्यारे देश सेवक,

मैंने लाल किले से पंचप्रण की बात कही थी। इस पंच प्रण ने देश को अपने आत्म गौरव की ओर लेकर के आगे बढ़ने का, लक्ष्यों को पार करने के सामर्थ्य के साथ आगे बढ़ने का एक बहुत बड़ा संबल दिया है। हमें गुलामी की मानसिकता हर पल मिटाते ही रहना है। जिस भारत का सपना नेताजी सुभाष चंद्र बोस ने देखा था, बाबा साहब आंबेडकर ने देखा था, पंडित नेहरू ने देखा था, सरदार पटेल, भगत सिंह, सुखदेव राजगुरु ने देखा था, डॉक्टर श्यामा प्रसाद मुखर्जी ने देखा था, भगवान बिरसा मुंडा ने देखा था, ज्योतिबा फुले ने देखा था, उन सब से प्रेरणा लेकर के हम आगे बढ़े। आइए इस संकल्प को हम दोहराए। स्वयं से ऊपर राष्ट्र का हित हो। स्वयं से ऊपर राष्ट्र का हित हो और कर्तव्य ही हमारी पहचान हो। मैं सभी देशवासियों से कहूंगा समय हमारा है, मैं सभी देशवासियों से कहूंगा समय हमारा है, अवसर हमारा है, संकल्प हमारा है, आइए सपनों को संकल्प बनाएं, संकल्प को सामर्थ्य बनाएं और सामर्थ्य को सफलता में बदल के रहें। आइए हर कदम को विकास का कदम बनाएं, कदम से कदम मिलाएं, मन से मन मिलाए, लक्ष्य से जुड़े रहे, एक दीप से जले दीप हजारों, आओ मिलकर विकसित भारत बनाएं। इसी एक भावना के साथ इस मंगल पर्व पर आप सबको अनेक-अनेक शुभकामनाएं।

Prime Minister Narendra Modi delivered the 80th Independence Day address from the Red Fort on 15 August 2026, outlining a national resolve to achieve a "Viksit Bharat" (Developed India) by 2047, the centenary of independence, while highlighting transformative progress across economic, social, and infrastructure sectors over the preceding 12 years.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
- **Occasion & Historic First**: 80th Independence Day address (15 August 2026); first time *Vande Mataram* was sung at the Red Fort on 15 August since independence, coinciding with the 150th anniversary of the song.
- **National Vision**: Target to become a developed nation by 2047 (100 years of independence), driven by 140 crore citizens.
- **Disaster Response**: Acknowledged recent floods and landslides affecting multiple regions; assured full government and national support to affected families.
- **Poverty Reduction**: 25 crore citizens lifted out of poverty over the last 12 years.
- **Economic Transformation**: Transitioned from "Fragile Five" status (pre-2014) to the fastest-growing major economy.
- **Sectoral Growth (12-year comparison)**:
  - Defence production: ~4x increase.
  - Khadi and Village Industries production: ~5x increase.
  - Electronics manufacturing: ~7x increase.
  - Modern railway coach production: 21x increase.
  - Mobile phone production: 35x increase.
  - Internet users/consumers: ~4x increase.
  - Patent grants: 4x increase.
  - Digital transactions: 100x increase.
- **Social Infrastructure Delivery (Annual Average Pace)**:
  - Tap water connections (Har Ghar Jal): 15x faster.
  - Gas connections: 6x faster.
  - Toilet construction for the poor: 4x faster.
  - Housing for the poor: 3x faster.
- **Governance Reforms**: Thousands of compliances eliminated; hundreds of obsolete laws repealed.
- **Infrastructure Expansion**: Significant expansion of metro networks and strengthening of public transport.
- **Closing Theme**: Emphasized self-confidence, self-pride, and *Atmanirbhar Bharat* (Self-Reliant India) as essential pillars for the 2047 goal.

headline: From 25 crore to 100 crore in a decade: Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlights India's record social security expansion
fullText:
Ministry of Labour & Employment

From 25 crore to 100 crore in a decade: Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlights India's record social security expansion

New avenues of employment and entrepreneurship for the youth over the past decade, says PM

15 AUG 2026 5:53PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address from the ramparts of the Red Fort today, highlighted the unprecedented expansion in India's social security coverage, noting that the number of people covered has increased from 25 crore before 2014 to 100 crore within a decade.

The Prime Minister said that the resolve for a developed India would be fulfilled only when development reaches the last person. Underlining the expansion of social security coverage, he said, “Before 2014, only 25 crore people had social security cover. He further added, “Only 25 crores in the last 5-7 decades; we have provided social security cover to 100 crore countrymen within a decade.”

Emphasising upon the benefits reaching families through social security and welfare measures, the Prime Minister also referred to the Ayushman Bharat scheme, under which elderly persons above 70 years of age are receiving free treatment up to ₹5 lakh.

The Prime Minister highlighted the significant progress made in creating new avenues of employment and entrepreneurship for the youth over the past decade. He noted that the Startup India initiative has enabled the growth of more than 2.5 lakh registered startups, with young entrepreneurs not only creating opportunities for themselves but also generating employment for others. He further underlined the role of the ₹1 lakh crore Innovation Fund, Skill India, Digital India, the opening up of the space and aviation sectors, and the National Drone Policy in creating new opportunities for employment, skilling and entrepreneurship. The expansion of airports, new air routes, aircraft manufacturing, maintenance and overhauling is also generating employment for skilled workers, the Prime Minister said.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi reiterated that ensuring that the benefits of development reach the last person remains central to the vision of a Viksit Bharat.

headline: DHR-ICMR celebrates 80th Independence Day with renewed commitment to health research, medical innovation and nation-building
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

DHR-ICMR celebrates 80th Independence Day with renewed commitment to health research, medical innovation and nation-building

15 AUG 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Health Research (DHR) and Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) celebrated the 80th Independence Day today at ICMR Headquarters, V. Ramalingaswami Bhawan, New Delhi, with patriotic fervour and a renewed commitment to advancing medical research, innovation and healthcare technologies for a Viksit Bharat.

Dr Rajiv Bahl, Secretary, Department of Health Research and Director General, ICMR, hoisted the National Flag at the ICMR Headquarters in the presence of senior DHR-ICMR officials, including Ms Richa Khoda, Joint Secretary, DHR, and Mr Vivek Kumar Daksh, Sr DDG (Administration), along with scientists, researchers and staff members.

Addressing the gathering on the occasion, Dr Rajiv Bahl underscored the critical role of health research and innovation in strengthening the nation’s development and healthcare ecosystem.

“Our work at ICMR is not merely a job; it is a contribution to nation-building. Through medical research, innovation and health technologies, we are helping build a Viksit Bharat—and a Bharat that can become a global leader in medical research and innovation.”

He emphasised that scientific excellence, innovation and the development of indigenous health technologies are essential to building a resilient and self-reliant healthcare system. He called upon the ICMR fraternity to continue working towards solutions that can improve healthcare accessibility and address the evolving health needs of the country.

As part of the Independence Day celebrations, a Prize Distribution Ceremony was also organised. Prizes were presented to the winners of the Essay Writing and Quiz Competitions conducted earlier this month. The competitions were organised to encourage creativity, knowledge, active participation and a spirit of engagement among DHR-ICMR officials and staff.

The celebrations concluded with a renewed call to the scientific and administrative fraternity to strive for excellence in biomedical research, foster innovation and contribute towards Aatmanirbharta in health technologies, while strengthening India’s position as a global leader in medical research and healthcare innovation.

headline: SURYAPATH TIRANGA GLOBAL RELAY Has Already Covered 40 Countries
fullText:
Ministry of Culture

SURYAPATH TIRANGA GLOBAL RELAY Has Already Covered 40 Countries

15 AUG 2026 5:01PM by PIB Delhi

The SURYAPATH TIRANGA Global Relay is live, marking a unique global celebration of India’s Independence Day as the Tiranga travels across the world following the path of the rising sun.

The Suryapath Tiranga journey began at 1:30 AM IST in Suva, Fiji, as the Tiranga was hoisted at the first point of the relay. From Fiji, the symbolic journey followed the path of the rising sun, moving westward across New Zealand, Australia, Japan, the Republic of Korea, China, Indonesia, Vietnam, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Myanmar. At every mission and post, the National Flag was hoisted, creating a continuous visual relay of the Tiranga across time zones and continents. By 8:00 AM, the journey had reached Bangladesh, followed by Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka and the Maldives, carrying the message of India's pride and unity across the region.

The relay continued westward through Uzbekistan and Oman, reaching the United Arab Emirates at 9:45 AM and finally Qatar at 10:30 AM IST. In just nine hours, the Tiranga travelled symbolically from the earliest light of day in the Pacific to West Asia, connecting 21 countries and missions/posts through one shared national symbol. Suryapath Tiranga thus transformed the rising sun into a global relay of patriotism—showing that wherever the sun rises, the spirit of the Tiranga follows, connecting Indians and friends of India across the world in the celebration of Har Ghar Tiranga 2026.

Speaking on this very special initiative under Har Ghar Tiranga 2026, Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture said “Suryapath Tiranga carries the spirit of India across the world through our nation’s powerful symbol—the Tiranga. Following the path of the rising sun, this unique relay connects our missions and the Indian diaspora in a shared celebration of India’s unity, heritage and democratic values. It is an invitation to Indians everywhere to come together and to share with the world the enduring spirit of Bharat.”

Suryapath Tiranga: The Journey Continues Across West Asia, Africa, Europe and the Americas

From 10:45 AM IST onwards, the Suryapath Tiranga continued its westward journey, moving across Kuwait, Saudi Arabia, Ethiopia, Russia, Kenya, Israel, Egypt and South Africa. With each successive flag hoisting, the Tiranga traversed a new time zone and geography, carrying the spirit of India's Independence Day across West Asia, Africa and Eurasia. By 12:30 PM IST, the relay had reached Pretoria, symbolically linking the Indian tricolour with the diverse landscapes and communities of the African continent.

The journey then moved into Europe, with the Tiranga being hoisted successively in Latvia, Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands, France, the United Kingdom, Spain, Morocco and Iceland. From Riga at 12:45 PM to Reykjavik at 3:00 PM IST, the relay created a remarkable chain of celebrations across Europe, demonstrating the global reach of India's national flag and the shared enthusiasm of Indian missions and communities abroad.

As the Suryapath Tiranga moved further west, the journey crossed the Atlantic towards the Americas, with the next scheduled stops being Brasilia, Brazil at 4:30 PM IST and Paramaribo, Suriname at 4:45 PM IST. From its first hoisting in Fiji at 1:30 AM to its onward journey across the Americas, the Tiranga has transformed the movement of the sun into a powerful global relay—one flag, carried symbolically across continents, connecting Indians and friends of India around the world on Independence Day.

Shri Randhir Jaiswal, Additional Secretary, XPD Division, MEA reflecting upon this special initiative under Har Ghar Tiranga said – “The Surya Path Tiranga campaign is a unique way to celebrate our freedom across the world. We are in the middle of this special relay celebration, which started from Fiji and has now crossed Suriname and will end at San Francisco in the US. The enthusiasm and participation from our Embassies, Consulates and people everywhere have made this a very special journey.”

headline: Key highlights of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s address from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day
fullText:
Prime Minister's Office

Key highlights of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s address from the ramparts of the Red Fort on the occasion of the 80th Independence Day

15 AUG 2026 4:44PM by PIB Delhi

Today, we are celebrating the 80th Independence Day. Today, the heartbeat of every Indian resonates with the chant of Vande Mataram.

Today, ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Hai, Har Man Tiranga Hai’ (the Tricolour is in every home and the Tricolour is in every heart). With enthusiasm and excitement, the nation is moving forward today with new resolutions.

Today, the nation fondly remembers those great sons and daughters of the soil who made the supreme sacrifice for the freedom of the country. Through their penance, sacrifice and dedication, they devoted their entire lives to the single goal of independence.

I respectfully salute all the freedom fighters, including revered Bapu, and the great revolutionaries who inspired this noble tradition of sacrifice.

For the first time since Independence, Vande Mataram is resonating from the Red Fort on 15 August. And today, when we are celebrating 150 years of Vande Mataram, what could be a more auspicious occasion than this?

In recent days, several parts of the country have witnessed severe floods and landslides, affecting numerous families. We deeply understand and share their pain and suffering. I assure the affected families that we, and the entire nation, stand firmly with them.

A nation becomes great and achieves its aspirations when it moves forward on the strength of its dreams, its resolve and its capabilities.

Our aspirations, too, must be lofty. Because when our dreams are lofty and our resolve is strong, the heights of our capabilities also rise, the scale of our efforts also expands, and only then can we turn our dreams into reality.

Today, Bharat too has envisioned a very big dream. It has envisioned it with firm resolve, with the aim of reaching new heights. And that dream is this: when the country completes 100 years of Independence, we will build a ‘Viksit Bharat’ (Developed India) in 2047.

We have to achieve this goal through the hard work and determination of 140 crore citizens. And when the world's most populous nation resolves to become a developed nation, it becomes a reflection of our courage in the eyes of the world as well. The world is compelled to change the way it looks at us.

Over the past 12 years, crores of citizens of the country, whether Dalits, the oppressed, the deprived, tribals, those living in villages or cities, the poor or the middle class, the youth or the elderly, women or men, people from the North or South, East or West, everyone has made every possible effort to take the nation to new heights with resolve and dedication.

I respectfully acknowledge and honour their efforts. And it is the result of these efforts that 25 crore citizens have overcome poverty and moved out of poverty in such a short period of time.

It is the result of the efforts of these citizens that we were once counted among the Fragile Five. Yet, within just 12 years, we have emerged as the fastest-growing economy among the major economies of the world.

Over the past 12 years, defence production has increased nearly fourfold. Production in the Khadi and Village Industries sector has increased nearly fivefold. Electronics manufacturing has grown nearly sevenfold.

The production of modern railway coaches has increased 21-fold. Mobile phone production has increased 35-fold. And not only that, even in the world of digital technology and innovation, we have made our mark keeping pace with the demands of the modern era.

The number of internet users and internet consumers has increased nearly fourfold. The number of patents granted has increased fourfold.

Digital transactions have increased 100-fold. At the same time, we have worked with equal seriousness towards improving the everyday convenience and quality of life of ordinary citizens.

Every year, we have provided tap-water connections at an average rate 15 times faster than before.

Every year, gas connections have been provided at an average rate six times faster. Every year, the construction of toilets for the poor has progressed at a rate four times faster. And every year, the pace of providing homes to the poor has increased threefold.

The country has brought about significant changes in governance as well. Thousands of compliances have been eliminated. Hundreds of outdated laws have been repealed. We cannot march into the 21st century with laws belonging to the previous century.

We have expanded metro networks for modern infrastructure and strengthened public transport. The speed at which we have worked, and the scale at which we have worked, this pace, this expansion and these achievements are something that Bharat has witnessed for the first time since Independence over the past decade.

And when we have so many achievements before us, when such rapid progress is visible, and when the capabilities of our citizens are growing stronger with every passing moment, then our resolve for a ‘Viksit Bharat’ by 2047 can never remain unfulfilled.

2. Ministry of Commerce and Industry

We too have to enhance our capabilities and safeguard our own interests. That is why we are moving forward with a very firm resolve to build ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ (a self-reliant India). Today, the hearts and minds of every Indian are becoming connected with initiatives like Make in India, Swadeshi, Vocal for Local etc.

Since 2014, we have been entering into Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) with nearly 40 countries around the world. Just look at the tremendous opportunity that has opened up. These trade agreements represent a very significant opportunity, and therefore, I especially want to tell our MSMEs: we must not let this opportunity pass us by.

We have to reach the world. Every Indian product must find its place in global markets. Whether it is our textiles, our machinery or our medicines, we must seize every opportunity. But we also have to meet and surpass global standards and parameters. We must offer the world something better than what we receive from it.

We have embarked on the Reform Express, and in the days ahead, we are going to move towards the next level of reforms. Therefore, everyone, including the government, society, industry, producers, farmers, will have to reform their traditional systems. We will have to reform our thinking and reform our goals as well.

When I speak of the ‘Sapt Dhara’ (seven streams of strength) in the days ahead, the first of these is the power of manufacturing.

We have to take the manufacturing sector to much greater heights. Along with increasing production, we must manufacture both the smallest components and the largest products.

The entire value chain must be ours. We need to move forward with that vision. We need the components, and we need complete manufacturing. We need to produce the complete product as well. From design to manufacturing, Bharat must become a trusted hub of the global supply chain.

Our factories must be competitive. Our products must be user-friendly. Our packaging must be appealing and attractive to people around the world. Zero-defect, precision manufacturing should become our identity.

I want to say to every manufacturer, every entrepreneur and every MSME: our identity in the global market must be built on reliability and quality. There can be no compromise on quality. And therefore, our mantra must be: Quality, Quality, Quality. This is what will become the foundation of our global brand value.

3. Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare

The government is shouldering a huge burden. A bag of urea that costs us 3,000 rupees in the global market is being made available to our farmers for just 300 rupees.

Not only that, the price of DAP in the global market has now reached 5,000 rupees, but we are still providing DAP at 1,350 rupees so that the farmers of my country do not face any difficulty.

The second stream of strength of this ‘Sapt Dhara’ is agriculture and food production. We have to move forward in the direction of food processing as well. The global markets are now opening up for our farmers.

Because of the FTAs, we are gaining access to a very large market. We have to reach those markets; we have to establish our presence there. We have to move from the farm all the way to the export market.

Our farmers should give greater emphasis to chemical-free farming, as the demand for such products is going to increase around the world. When our agricultural products meet and fulfil global parameters in every respect, we will be able to access global markets with ease.

4. Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

Mobile phone production has increased 35-fold. And not only that, even in the world of digital technology and innovation, we have made our mark keeping pace with the demands of the modern era.

Digital transactions have increased 100-fold. At the same time, we have worked with equal seriousness to improve the convenience and quality of life of ordinary citizens.

In today's digital world and in today's era of technology, we understand the significance of the chip. Whether it is an electronic product, medical equipment, or our transportation systems, chips are indispensable everywhere.

We have reached a point where the entire world could come to a standstill without chips. That is why, Bharat has taken major steps towards semiconductor manufacturing in the direction of becoming self-reliant. Three semiconductor plants have already been initiated.

I want to tell the people of the country that in the coming seven to eight years, another five to eight semiconductor plants are expected to be established very soon. This journey towards ‘Aatmanirbhar Bharat’ provides us with a highway towards becoming a ‘Viksit Bharat’.

The third stream of strength of my ‘Sapt Dhara’ is technology and innovation. Today is the age of AI, quantum technology, space, robotics and data centres. An entirely new field has opened up before us.

Emerging technologies are also challenging us at every moment. Therefore, we must not merely turn Bharat into a market for the world; we must make Bharat a hub of innovation.

We have demonstrated our capabilities and established our credentials through UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure. Now, Bharat must take its Digital Public Technologies to every corner of the world. Bharat must take the lead in next-generation communication technologies.

Our goal should be to ensure that Made-in-India 6G reaches every corner of the world. We must accelerate our efforts in this direction, and our commitment and endeavour must not diminish.

5. Ministry of Mines

We have launched the National Critical Minerals Mission with the objective of securing critical minerals for the country. We also announced the Critical Minerals Corridor in the Budget.

We are entering into agreements with several countries, and many nations around the world are now beginning to place their trust in Bharat when it comes to critical minerals.

6. Ministry of Power / Ministry of New and Renewable Energy

It is becoming increasingly difficult to run the new world without energy. Whether it is chips, AI or data centres, we will need enormous amounts of electricity.

Energy security is the need of our times, and that is why we have already taken one strong step after another in this direction.

One major means of ensuring energy security is nuclear energy. By passing the SHANTI Act in Parliament, we have paved the way towards a new goal. By 2047, we are working towards a target of 100 GW of nuclear power capacity.

Before 2014, piped gas was reaching barely 20-22 lakh households. Today, we are providing piped gas to nearly 1.75 crore households.

Twelve years ago, the country’s solar energy capacity was only 2 GW—just 2 GW. Today, we have achieved a capacity of 160 GW.

We launched the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, and today I am pleased to say that, in such a short period, we have already crossed the milestone of 50 lakh households adopting solar energy. The programme is progressing rapidly, and as a result, the electricity bills of thousands of households have effectively become zero.

Thousands of households are also earning income by selling the surplus electricity they generate after meeting their own requirements. The government is providing 80,000 rupees in assistance to each family for this initiative, and with this support, we are moving towards completing this transformation.

The sixth stream of strength in our Sapt Dhara is the Green Economy and Blue Economy, which will also create green jobs.

We must achieve global-scale leadership in green hydrogen, renewable energy, energy storage, green mobility and green manufacturing. We have to establish ourselves as a global leader in all these areas.

7. Department of Atomic Energy

Over this decade itself, we are working towards the goal of commissioning five new nuclear reactors. This year, Bharat has crossed a significant milestone by mastering Fast Breeder Reactor technology. As a result, we have taken a major step forward towards becoming self-reliant in nuclear fuel.

8. Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

Before 2014, that is, 12 years ago, piped gas distribution was available in only 70 cities across the country. In these 12 years, we have expanded that network from 70 cities to 700 cities. This is what speed looks like. This is what expansion looks like. Every year, gas connections have been provided at an average rate six times faster.

Before 2014, piped gas reached barely 20-22 lakh households. Today, we are providing piped gas to 1.75 crore households. Twelve years ago, the country’s solar energy capacity was only 2 GW—just 2 GW. Today, we have achieved a capacity of 160 GW.

9. Ministry of Railways

The production of modern railway coaches has increased 21-fold. The electrification of our railway network began in 1925. Yet, over the following 90 years—from 1925 to 2015—only about 30% of the railway network had been electrified.

We completed the remaining work in just one decade, achieving near-total electrification. 30% in 90 years, 70% in 10 years and this is what progress looks like.

As a result, we have reduced our dependence on diesel, which we have to import from abroad. Our trains are increasingly running on electricity, bringing significant benefits to the environment.

The country has also introduced its first hydrogen-powered train. I am pleased that it is the longest and most powerful hydrogen-powered train, and that Bharat has also established its leadership in the field of hydrogen trains globally.

10. Ministry of Home Affairs

Naxalism and Maoism have destroyed the future of millions of young people. For four long decades, Naxalism held large parts of the country and a vast section of its population in its grip, keeping them under the threat of the gun. It tore the Constitution to shreds, and in the effort to protect ordinary citizens of the country, more than 3,500 of our police and security personnel made the supreme sacrifice.

Today, I am pleased that Naxalite-Maoist violence is perhaps no longer even capable of taking its final breath. In places where Naxalites once fired their guns, where the soil was once stained with blood, today, in those very Naxal-affected regions, the Tricolour of development, trust and endeavour is flying high because these areas are becoming Naxal-free.

The armed Naxalites have been defeated, but the Naxal mindset remains. These forces are looking for opportunities. They are searching for paths of violence and anarchy, and are employing various tactics to drag society onto the wrong path.

We must identify this Naxal mindset. We must isolate such elements and connect the country's young generation with the mainstream path of building a developed nation.

Building a secure Bharat is the responsibility of all of us. Whether the challenge comes from within our borders or from across the frontier, Bharat is prepared for every eventuality. The nature of warfare is changing today. There is no longer any guarantee that a war will take place only on the battlefield or along the border.

Today, I am announcing from the Red Fort that in the days ahead, we will build a vibrant civil defence network. We will equip our citizens and civil defence personnel with modern systems and technologies and familiarise them with contemporary methods of preparedness.

11. Ministry of Defence

Our fifth stream of strength of the Sapt Dhara is defence power. The importance of defence strength is undeniable in every respect. Bharat has now realised, and the world has also recognised, that there is no alternative to becoming self-reliant in defence.

We must set ourselves the goal of developing next-generation defence technologies and moving towards becoming a global defence supplier. We must develop drones and counter-drone systems, and we must take the lead in hypersonic defence technologies.

Cybersecurity is also becoming a challenge for every household today. This too is an area of defence in which we can harness the capabilities of our youth and use their talent for the benefit of both the nation and the world.

We had announced Mission Sudarshan Chakra in recent years, and work on it is progressing at a very rapid pace. Today, our defence exports have increased nearly 50-fold, and our weapons and defence equipment are reaching around 100 countries across the world.

12. Ministry of Road Transport and Highways

The fourth strength of the Sapt Dhara (seven streams) is Gati Shakti. Under Gati Shakti, we must focus on seamless and fast connectivity within the country.

We must connect our cities through high-speed rail. We need modern highways, inland waterways, airports and a multimodal logistics system.

13. Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways

We must not view our ports merely as places for loading and unloading goods, or simply as places where ships from around the world come and anchor. We must take our ports forward in the direction of port-led development and growth.

Bharat also has a tremendous opportunity in the blue economy. We have a very long coastline, and there are enormous opportunities in the blue economy.

There are fisheries, coastal tourism, ocean technology and many other areas in which we can move forward.

14. Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying

From Keralam to Gujarat and from Tamil Nadu to Bengal, along our coastline, our fisherfolk have seen a significant increase in the potential for exporting our shrimp as a result of this FTA. The potential for our seafood to reach markets across the world has also increased.

Bharat also has a tremendous opportunity in the blue economy. We have a very long coastline, and there are enormous opportunities in the blue economy. There are fisheries, coastal tourism, ocean technology and many other areas in which we can move forward.

15. Ministry of Tourism

Bharat possesses vast wildlife resources. We have more than 100 national parks. The potential is immense, but we have fallen short when it comes to attracting foreign tourists. We have an opportunity to use our soft power to attract tourists from across the world to Bharat. We must showcase our potential to the world.

Today, sports are also a major source of attraction towards Bharat. Why should the world's sporting events not be held in Bharat? The concert economy is growing rapidly and is a major attraction for the country's youth.

Every artist in the world wants to perform in Bharat at some point. This is a tremendous opportunity, and we must create the necessary infrastructure and systems to mobilise it.

16. Ministry of Culture / Ministry of Textiles

Our seventh stream is Bharat's soft power. This is the strength of Bharat's soft power. Today, yoga has connected the entire world with Bharat. Yoga is increasingly becoming a source of energy for the world.

Bharat has centres of faith, Ayurveda and a holistic healthcare system. With the Heal in India movement, we can take Bharat's capabilities to the world.

Whether it is handicrafts, culture, our films, our creative world, VFX, animation, gaming or digital content, Bharat can showcase its stature in the creative world.

Today, Bharat has given tremendous strength to the WAVES Summit. Gradually, the world looks forward to Bharat's World Audio Visual and Entertainment Summit, which will introduce Bharat's soft power and creative world to the global audience.

17. Ministry of Finance / Department of Financial Services

It is the result of the efforts of our fellow citizens that, once counted among the Fragile Five, we have become a major economy and the fastest-growing major economy within 12 years

A nation does not comprise only the government; every citizen is a part of the nation. Why can we not aspire to have 50 Indian companies among the Fortune 500 within the next decade? Why should this not be our goal?

We have demonstrated our capabilities and established our credentials through UPI and Digital Public Infrastructure. Digital transactions have increased 100-fold. Now, Bharat must take its Digital Public Technologies to every corner of the world. Bharat must take the lead in next-generation communication technologies.

Today, the banking sector is flourishing. Why should the flag of an Indian bank not fly among the world's top banks? An Indian bank should also be among the world's top five banks.

Nearly 3.25 crore families have benefited from the SVAMITVA Scheme, and as a result, assets worth around ₹140 lakh crore have been unlocked. This can enable people to obtain loans from banks and start their own businesses.

18. Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

We have done a great deal of work in the pharmaceutical sector. However, the need of the hour is for one or two Indian pharmaceutical companies to feature among the world's five largest pharmaceutical companies.

Over the past five to seven decades, only 25 crore people had been covered, whereas within a single decade, we have provided a social security cover to 100 crore citizens.

Under the Ayushman Bharat Scheme, even senior citizens aged 70 years and above are now being provided free medical treatment and medicines worth up to ₹5 lakh.

19. Ministry of Education

We have opened up the space sector. We have formulated the National Drone Policy. We have introduced the Khelo India Policy. There had been no new education policy for 35 years; we have brought in a new National Education Policy, and middle-class families have benefited from it.

Between 2004 and 2014, there were fewer than 350 universities in our country. Today, within 10–12 years, nearly 650 new universities have been added. We are approaching the figure of 1,000 universities.

Before 2014, there were only around 400 medical seats; today, there are nearly 850 medical seats. Not only that, foreign universities are now also coming to Bharat. Arrangements have been made to enable our young people to obtain degrees from foreign universities while studying in Bharat.

We are working to ensure that the young minds of our country develop an interest in technology from childhood. That is why we have placed more than 10,000 Atal Tinkering Labs at the disposal of young children, so that they can develop an interest in innovation and technology.

We have decided to provide free online coaching for various examinations to our youth. We have digital public infrastructure and excellent talent and teachers. By bringing these resources together, we are going to establish a complete network to provide free coaching to the country's youth.

20. Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports

Young people have a very important role to play in the journey towards a 'Viksit Bharat' (developed India). Not only that, the youth of my country will also be the greatest beneficiaries of a developed Bharat.

Therefore, we must take forward the goal of a developed India by connecting it with our youth. We must move forward by making our youth our highest priority.

A great deal has happened in this direction over the past 10–12 years. The Startup India campaign has now resulted in more than 2.5 lakh registered start-ups across the country.

The youth of our country are not only creating employment for themselves but are also providing employment to many others.

The Government has announced an Innovation Fund of ₹1 lakh crore. I want to tell the youth of the country: bring your dreams to us; we will ensure that there is no shortage of resources.

New opportunities for research and affordable data through Digital India have empowered our youth.

Indian private start-ups, founded by young people with an average age of 28, have already launched their satellites and rockets on their very first trials, achieving a remarkable feat.

Today, there are more than 2.5 lakh registered start-ups. We recently held the AI Impact Summit. The expansion of AI is taking place at a very rapid pace.

From the ramparts of the Red Fort, I want to make an announcement for the youth of the country. We have decided that, during the next one year, we will train 1 crore young people in AI skills, so that the youth of our country have the capability to lead in the world of AI as well.

The country's youth have demonstrated their capabilities in the bioeconomy. Before 2014, the sector had a turnover of ₹60,000 crore; today, our bioeconomy has reached ₹20 lakh crore, friends.

The TOPS scheme has achieved tremendous success. Khelo India Games, University Games, Winter Games, Beach Games, sports infrastructure, coaching for sports, sports medicine and sports nutrition — in all these areas, Bharat is now moving towards achieving excellence.

Bharat's performance in the world of sports is improving, and we are moving forward as strong contenders for the 2036 Olympics. Bharat is also set to host the Commonwealth Games in 2030.

We want the 2036 Olympics to be held in Bharat too. But in 2036, there will be sporting events in which Bharat does not compete today, or does not qualify, and events from which India has remained absent.

Three-quarters of the opportunities are still awaiting us. Bharat will focus on these areas, and for this, we also want to launch a talent-hunt campaign.

A talent-hunt campaign will be conducted across villages, cities and schools to identify sporting talent among children aged between 5 and 15. Their talent will be assessed, and they will then be given special training to develop them into accomplished athletes who can represent the country.

For the country and for the youth of the country, drug addiction is becoming a major challenge. A Drug-Free India (Nasha Mukt Bharat) should be a collective responsibility for all of us.

21. Department of Space

The third strength of my 'Sapta Dhara' is technology and innovation. Today is the era of AI, quantum technology, space, robotics, and data centers; an entirely new frontier has opened up.

Emerging technologies are constantly challenging us; therefore, we must not let the country merely become a market for the world—we must become a hub of innovation.

We have opened up the space sector. We have formulated the National Drone Policy and the Khelo India Policy. There had been no education policy for 35 years, but we introduced a new education policy, and middle-class families have benefited from it.

22. Ministry of Women and Child Development

The contribution of our sisters and daughters in nation-building today remains a great source of inspiration for all of us. Whether in fighter jets or civil aviation, our daughters are at the forefront.

We had set a target of making 3 crore sisters 'Lakhpati Didis,' and we have surpassed that goal. Now we are moving ahead with the goal of creating 6 crore Lakhpati Didis. The creation of 3 crore new Lakhpati Didis signifies a massive transformation in the rural economy driven by the power of women.

Today, standing here beneath the shadow of the Tricolour on the ramparts of the Red Fort, I appeal to and urge all the political parties of the country to come forward in honour of women and ensure that our mothers and sisters secure 33% representation in the Legislative Assemblies and the Lok Sabha as soon as possible, so that they may contribute to shaping India's policies.

It is the need of the hour and I once again urge all the political parties, come and join in the cause of women's respect by implementing women reservation, you also take the fame, you also take the credit, but give rights to my mothers and sisters.

23. Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment

I respectfully acknowledge these efforts; it is a result of this that, in such a short span of time, 25 crore citizens have overcome poverty and risen out of it.

While only 25 crore people were lifted out of poverty over the past 5–7 decades, we have provided a protective shield of social security to 100 crore citizens within just a single decade.

We had set a target of making 3 crore sisters 'Lakhpati Didis,' and we have surpassed that goal. Now we are moving ahead with the goal of creating 6 crore Lakhpati Didis.

The creation of 3 crore new Lakhpati Didis signifies a massive transformation in the rural economy driven by the power of women.

Every year, the work of building toilets for the poor was done at four times the speed.

The work of providing houses to the poor was done at three times the speed every year.

Under the Ayushman Bharat scheme, free medical treatment worth up to Rs 5 lakh is now being provided even to elderly citizens aged 70 and above.

24. Ministry of Tribal Affairs

Over the past 12 years, countless citizens across the country—whether Dalits, the oppressed, the deprived, or tribals; residents of villages or cities; the poor or the middle class; youth or the elderly; women or men; and people from the North, South, East, or West—have all strived in every possible way to take the nation to new heights, driven by a shared resolve and dedication.

25. Ministry of Rural Development

We have provided tap water connections at an average rate 15 times faster than before. Gas connections were given to people at an average speed of six times more every year.

Every year, the work of building toilets for the poor was done at four times the speed. The work of providing houses to the poor was done at three times the speed every year.

We had set a target of empowering 3 crore sisters to become 'Lakhpati Didis', and we have surpassed that goal. Now, we are moving forward with the target of creating 6 crore 'Lakhpati Didis'.

The creation of 3 crore new 'Lakhpati Didis' signifies a massive transformation in the rural economy driven by women's power.

26. Ministry of Jal Shakti

On average, we have provided tap water connections 15 times faster each year.

27. Ministry of Civil Aviation

The aviation sector is also growing rapidly for my young people. New airports, new routes, and new employment avenues are being generated.

Activities related to maintenance and overhauling are providing jobs to a vast pool of skilled manpower across the country.

We have achieved success in the direction of manufacturing 'Made in India' aircraft.

The 'Made in India' C295 Defence Transport aircraft has already completed its successful flight.

28. Department of Science and Technology

The Government of India has announced an innovation fund of Rs 1 lakh crore. I want to tell the youth of the country, come with your dreams, we will not let there be any shortage of resources.

New opportunities for research and the availability of affordable data under 'Digital India' have empowered the youth.

29. Department of Biotechnology

The country's youth power has demonstrated its potential in the bio-economy. Friends, the bio-economy, which stood at a turnover of Rs 60,000 crore prior to 2014 has today reached Rs 20 lakh crore.

30. Ministry of Heavy Industries

Back in 2009-10, only 1.5 lakh electric vehicles were sold; in 2025-26, 25 lakh electric vehicles have been sold.

31. Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship

From the Red Fort, I wish to make an announcement for the youth of the country. We have decided that in the coming one year we will work to train 1 crore youth in AI skills so that the youth of our country have the ability to lead in the world of AI.

The aviation sector is also expanding rapidly, creating new opportunities for our youth. New airports and routes are generating fresh employment prospects.

Activities such as maintenance and overhauling are providing jobs to a vast number of skilled manpower across the country.

We have achieved success in manufacturing 'Made in India' aircraft; the 'Made in India' C295 Defence Transport aircraft has already completed its successful flight.

32. Ministry of Law and Justice

The country has brought about significant changes in governance as well. Thousands of compliance requirements have been eliminated, and hundreds of obsolete laws have been repealed. Laws from the last century cannot keep pace with the 21st century.

In this regard, I wish to tell state governments and local self-governing bodies—and it is the Government of India's responsibility too—that we must accelerate the pace of our reforms.

We must develop our systems to meet the vision of 2047. We cannot live by the policies and rules of the past. we must frame policies and rules that cater to the aspirations of the future.

33. Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation / Census of India

The Census process is underway, the count is ongoing, and counting is not just about numbers.

It is the nuances within this data that shape policies and plans, and enable the country to draft its roadmap for progress; therefore, having accurate information is crucial.

I urge the youth of the country to sit down with their family members and fully understand the form.

You see, the country will accomplish such a huge task and the country's time and energy will be utilized for the right work and hence I urge the youth of my country to actively participate in this work of census.

34. Ministry of Commerce and Industry / Department of Pharmaceuticals

We have done a great deal of work in the pharmaceutical sector. However, the need of the hour is for one or two Indian pharmaceutical companies to make their mark among the world's top five pharma companies.

Why shouldn't any of our consulting firms, accounting firms, be among the top firms in the world? Our goal should be to make Indian technology companies the leaders in the world.

We should have brands that attract the world. We must work towards making our brands the identity of our country and a destination for the world.

35. Developed India

A country is not just about the government; it is about every citizen. Can't we imagine that we hear a lot about Fortune 500. Why shouldn't we envision and set a goal, that within the coming decade, 50 of these Fortune 500 companies are from India?

We must develop our systems to meet the goals of 2047. We cannot rely on the policies and rules of the past, instead, we must frame policies that reflect our aspirations for the future.

I had spoken of the 'Panch Pran' (five pledges) from the Red Fort. These five pledges have provided immense strength to the nation, empowering it to move forward with a sense of self-pride and the capability to surpass its goals. We have to keep eradicating the mentality of slavery every moment.

The interest of the nation should be above self. The interest of the nation should be above our own and duty should be our identity. I would like to tell all my countrymen that the time is ours, the opportunity is ours, the resolve is ours, let us convert our dreams into resolve, resolve into strength and strength into success.

Let us make every step a step of development, let us join step with step, let our hearts join with our hearts, let us remain connected to the goal, one lamp will light thousands of lamps, let us together build a developed India.

headline: Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India launches RSVC-AMRIT platform developed by NABARD to strengthen rural innovation and technology transfer
fullText:
Office of Principal Scientific Advisor to GoI

Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India launches RSVC-AMRIT platform developed by NABARD to strengthen rural innovation and technology transfer

15 AUG 2026 4:30PM by PIB Delhi

Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, launched the RSVC AMRIT platform on 15th August 2025, the 80th Independence Day, marking a significant step towards strengthening technology-led rural development. Developed by NABARD in collaboration with the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser (OPSA) to the Government of India, AMRIT serves as the digital backbone of the RuTAGe Smart Village Centre (RSVC) ecosystem, supporting rural innovation and technology transfer and enabling wider adoption of appropriate technologies in rural areas. The launch event was attended by Dr. Shaji Krishnan V., Chairman, NABARD, along with representatives from various organisations and stakeholder groups.

In his address, Prof. Sood emphasised that AMRIT is designed as a comprehensive digital ecosystem supporting the complete RSVC lifecycle, from technology discovery and validation to deployment tracking, collaboration, monitoring and knowledge management. He said the platform will progressively bring together innovators, technology providers, startups, validators, accelerators, implementation partners, funding agencies, academic institutions and rural communities on a shared platform. By connecting these stakeholders, AMRIT is expected to strengthen collaboration and accelerate the dissemination of technologies in rural areas, helping take technology and innovation closer to the last mile.

Highlighting the need for the platform, Dr. Krishnan noted that while India has a rich ecosystem of scientific institutions, innovators, startups and technology providers, connecting appropriate technologies with rural needs remains a challenge. AMRIT seeks to bridge this gap by connecting rural needs with innovations, institutions and implementation mechanisms, strengthening technology dissemination and adoption at the grassroots level. He reaffirmed NABARD’s commitment to supporting such enterprises across the country, in addition to the 8 RSVCs currently being supported.

The RSVC initiative facilitates the transfer of appropriate and affordable technologies from research institutions, innovators and startups to rural communities through village-level technology hubs, covering areas such as agriculture, rural enterprises, renewable energy, education, assistive technologies, water and sanitation, and citizen services. AMRIT builds on this physical outreach by adding a digital layer to the ecosystem, with NABARD expecting it to evolve into a national repository of rural innovations, technologies, best practices and collaboration opportunities, supporting wider technology adoption and the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

The initiative builds on NABARD’s earlier tripartite MoU with OPSA and NABFOUNDATION, a subsidiary of NABARD, and the establishment of a Centre of Excellence on RSVCs at its head office in Mumbai. On the occasion, NABARD shared the broad contours of its scheme for establishing RSVCs, which will be supported by NABARD and set up in collaboration with corporates through CSR initiatives, with NABFOUNDATION serving as the implementation partner.

The launch event can be accessed on: https://www.youtube.com/live/PXitjx7p8eY?si=wBipNND88Czxfv-6

headline: DLI Scheme-backed Chip Design Startup - Aheesa Digital Innovations Achieved First-Pass Silicon Success With ‘VIHAAN’, a Broadband Chip Built Using the Indigenous VEGA Microprocessor
fullText:
Ministry of Electronics & IT

DLI Scheme-backed Chip Design Startup - Aheesa Digital Innovations Achieved First-Pass Silicon Success With ‘VIHAAN’, a Broadband Chip Built Using the Indigenous VEGA Microprocessor

VIHAAN Aims to Bring Fibre Broadband to Indian Homes and Has Attracted VC Funding from the Tamil Nadu Infrastructure Fund Management Corporation (TNIFMC) and Other Investors

DLI Scheme-backed Companies Have Cumulatively Raised Over $100 Million in VC Funding and Achieved 35 Design Tape-outs

15 AUG 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi

Semiconductor chip design is a critical value driver across the semiconductor value chain, contributing up to 50% of overall value addition and accounting for approximately 15–35% of the Bill of Materials (BOM) cost of electronic products.

Recognising the pivotal role of semiconductor design in the country’s strategic technological ambitions, the Design Linked Incentive (DLI) Scheme is supporting Indian Startups for designing chips for a wide range of strategic and commercial applications. These include satellite communications, drones, surveillance cameras, Defence and Aerospace Systems, Automotive, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, LED drivers, AI systems, Telecom Equipment, and Smart Meters.

Aheesa Digital Innovations

Headquartered in Chennai, Aheesa is an Indian fabless semiconductor startup that designs chips for broadband networking and security. Taped out on Republic Day and achieving first-pass silicon success on Independence Day this year, ‘VIHAAN’ - a networking System-on-Chip (SoC) purpose-built for Fibre Broadband- will now proceed towards production tape-out, targeted for 2027.

As India expands its digital infrastructure through optical fibre, 5G, and broadband-led services, the need for domestically designed semiconductor solutions is growing. Aheesa, through its VIHAAN series, successive funding milestones, and active support from the DLI Scheme, is positioned to serve this need.

Investor Confidence - Supporting India’s Deep-Tech Innovation to Scale Global Solutions

Earlier this year, Aheesa raised about ₹40 crore from TNIFMC through the Tamil Nadu Emerging Sector Seed Fund (TNESSF) and other private investors to accelerate product development and support the company’s growth in the semiconductor space. These successive rounds of funding after approval under the DLI Scheme reflects growing confidence of investors in Aheesa's ability to deliver advanced broadband silicon solutions from India.

Government support helping Indian chip companies move from idea to product

Aheesa’s achievement is part of a larger transformation taking place in India’s semiconductor design ecosystem. Through the Government’s semiconductor programmes, state-of-the-art chip-design tools made available to 455 organisations, including 350 academic institutions and 105 startups, enabling students, researchers and companies across the country to design chips.

Companies supported under the DLI Scheme have cumulatively achieved over 30 chip design tape-outs across various foundries and raised more than US$100 million in VC funding, demonstrating growing investor confidence in India’s semiconductor design capabilities. Under the Chips to Startup (C2S) Programme, 245 chip designs have been taped out by 71 academic institutions, to meet future workforce requirements.

Other recent successes under the Scheme

1. Vervesemi Microelectronics achieved first-pass silicon success of BLDC Motor Controller chip using indigenous microprocessor by Incore Semiconductor and its Motor Driver chip.

2. Netrasemi successfully tested 12nm Vision SoC with integrated video analytics acceleration.

3. OptoML received its 12nm ‘compute-in-memory’ SoC, which makes AI processing faster and power-efficient.

4. Mindgrove Technologies announced a partnership with PRAMA India to explore the usage of its Vision SoC in CCTV surveillance cameras.

5. IndieSemiC secured global certification for its Bluetooth (BLE 6) chip module.

Building an Indian semiconductor ecosystem

The Government’s semiconductor initiatives are aimed not merely at designing individual chips, but at building an ecosystem covering the entire semiconductor value chain — from chip design and manufacturing to advanced packaging, equipment, materials, research and development, and skilled manpower. With Semicon 2.0, approved with an outlay of ₹1,27,500 crore in July 2026, India is taking this effort to the next level, with the objective of building a globally competitive semiconductor ecosystem.

The progress of companies such as Aheesa Digital Innovations demonstrates that Indian semiconductor designs are increasingly moving beyond the laboratory. Chips designed in India are now being fabricated, tested, validated, and prepared for customer trials. As the ecosystem matures, silicon-validated designs will move towards volume manufacturing, positioning Indian companies as credible global suppliers while strengthening domestic supply chains and self-reliance.

headline: Lokpal of India Celebrates 80th Independence Day; Reaffirms Commitment to Clean and Corruption-Free Governance
fullText:
Lokpal of India Celebrates 80th Independence Day; Reaffirms Commitment to Clean and Corruption-Free Governance

15 AUG 2026 4:25PM by PIB Delhi

On the occasion of the 80th Independence Day of India, the National flag was hoisted by Hon’ble Shri Justice Ajay Manikrao Khanwilkar, Chairperson, Lokpal of India in the august presence of Hon’ble Members: Shri Justice Lingappa Narayana Swamy, Shri Justice Sanjay Yadav, Shri Sushil Chandra, Shri justice Ritu Raj Awasthi, Shri Pankaj Kumar and Shri Ajay Tirkey. He extended greetings of Independence Day to all Hon’ble Members, senior officers, staff and their family members.

Recalling the inspiring words of Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore, he emphasized the vision of a nation “where the mind is without fear and the head is held high.” Citizens were urged to reaffirm this ideal and uphold it in thought and action.

The address highlighted that India’s freedom is hard-earned, achieved through the immense sacrifices of freedom fighters and countless patriots whose courage continues to inspire future generations. The hoisting of the National Flag was described as not merely a ceremonial act but a solemn reminder of both the nation’s past and the responsibilities that accompany freedom. He stressed that true freedom means freedom from hunger, injustice, oppression, and inequality, and the opportunity for every citizen to live with dignity.

Special emphasis was laid on the role of the Lokpal of India as an institution committed to clean, and corruption free governance. The increasing number of complaints received by the Lokpal was viewed as a sign of growing citizen engagement and confidence in the institution.

He reaffirmed the Lokpal’s commitment to the Constitution, the rule of law, accountability, efficiency, transparency, and accessibility. He called for an institution that is efficient, transparent, accessible, and strengthened through the effective use of technology. He emphasised on the Lokpal’s fundamental purpose to serve the Constitution, to uphold the rule of law and to ensure that public authority is exercised with responsibility. All officials were urged to treat every complaint with seriousness, fairness, and objectivity, remembering that behind every file is a citizen seeking justice and a life affected by institutional decisions.

He concluded his speech by expressing sincere gratitude to the Hon’ble Members, officers, staff, and their families for their dedication and professionalism and thanked everyone for participating in the celebration. The speech ended with a patriotic call of “Jai Hind”.
